target_customer: music fans who buy songs and independent artists who sell them
problem: Fans who discover music early get no reward when it becomes popular. Popcuts paid early buyers a share of later sales of the same song.
business_model: marketplace take rate; Popcuts kept 10 to 20 percent of sales, artists chose their cut and the rest went to fans as site credit
product_category: online DRM free music store with fan revenue sharing

founders.name: Hannes Hesse
education: UC Berkeley School of Information, 2008 graduate (per school news item)
founders.background_notes: The Berkeley item says three 2008 graduates cofounded the store and names only Hesse, age 28. Not on the YC page. The other graduate cofounders are not identified and the item does not say which cofounder studied what.

exit.reason: No shutdown announcement found; YC lists the company as Inactive.

competitors.name: Amazon MP3
competitors.what: DRM free MP3 store at 89 to 99 cents per song
competitors.traction_then: public beta September 2007; Sony BMG catalog added January 2008

competitors.name: iTunes Plus (Apple)
competitors.what: DRM free songs sold by Apple, cut to 99 cents after Amazon's launch

technical_complexity.rationale: A payments, catalog and credit sharing system for songs with per song payout tracking is more than basic commerce, and artist onboarding was needed.

defensibility.rationale: The fan share mechanic was novel but easy to copy, and the catalog was small at launch, about 700 songs from about 200 artists per one report.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Apple and Amazon dominated DRM free sales by 2008; analysts quoted by the press were skeptical of a small store competing with them.

market_need_then: Digital downloads were rising and DRM was being dropped in 2007 and 2008, but the artist and fan revenue share idea had no documented demand beyond launch press.

branding.domain_note: popcuts.com exact match; the host returned 503 when fetched.
branding.brand_signature: Buyers earn a cut when later buyers purchase the same song
branding.community_and_virality: Associated Press story in September 2008 and a Hot 100 retail sites list from Internet Retailer in December 2008.

brand_strength.rationale: Name tied clearly to the revenue share idea and drew AP coverage, but no sign of a lasting community or loyal base.

outcome_analysis: Popcuts launched in August 2008 with a fan revenue share store out of Berkeley and won AP and trade press, but it faced Apple and Amazon at the same price and a thin catalog. YC lists it as Inactive and no source gives the cause or date of closure, so no failure factors are assigned.
notes: The Berkeley item and press snippets (take rate, catalog size, skeptical analysts) come from search result summaries of the AP story and school pages; only the Berkeley page was opened. Funding was not found in any source. Competitor sources predate the batch by under a year and describe market conditions at founding.
